title: graphite query result envelope v1
description: Common envelope for `graphite query` and `graphite query --natural` responses. Consume rule: branch on the presence of error_code first; success responses carry resolution (per-target, aligned with plan roles). Verb-specific payload keys (callers, calls, depends_on, imported_by, source/target/length/path, community, stats fields, ...) are additive and deliberately not constrained here. Bounded verbs report truncated + limits; a no_path error with truncated:true means the depth bound was hit, not that absence was proven. Note for consumers reusing graphite's subset validator (routing/schema_validation.py): it treats ABSENT additionalProperties as closed, so every deliberately open object in this file says additionalProperties:true explicitly.

resolution_health.description: Measured resolution-health block: placeholder_nodes, by_relation, by_language, healthy, threshold. Present on stats/impact/context/relation-verb results from 2026-07-25. Distinct from the top-level `resolution` array above, which is per-target input-match metadata, not graph-wide resolver health. schema 3: both `calls` and `imports` cells carry an `external` count of edges that leave the repo (confidence `EXTERNAL_CALL`/`EXTERNAL_IMPORT`); an edge counts as external only when it also failed to bind, and externals are excluded from ratios. Ratios are not comparable across schemas (1: includes all externals; 2: excludes only import externals; 3: excludes both) — branch on `schema`.

inconclusive.description: True when the result is empty AND the graph's resolution health is below threshold — treat as unknown, not as 'no dependents'.

answer.description: Answer-scoped confidence: relations walked, per-language health cells for exactly those, derived grade, applicable caveat codes; empty_meaning present iff the primary result is empty. Absent when the block could not be computed (fail-open) or on error results other than no_path.
